headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Kestra’s broad filesystem/network orchestration into LightZero’s isolated, non-writing runtime; prompt-injection and conflict risks are low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and pass messages, so if LightZero outputs are manually copied or stored in shared files, instruction-like content could be misread. LightZero has no filesystem write, network, or MCP surface, so the bridge is weak and not default. The pathway exists but is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies LightZero output into a Kestra task or shared file
IF Kestra parses that content as workflow instructions
mitigations: Keep LightZero output out of shared workflow files
Require a human review step before Kestra consumes model text
Prefix copied text with clear non-instruction delimiters
Use separate directories for model output and workflow definitions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and can egress broadly, so sensitive data could leave its workspace. LightZero is local-only with no network egress or filesystem read/write, so it is unlikely to leak on its own. The pair still creates a default leakage path through Kestra’s broad I/O surfaces.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows process sensitive inputs or artifacts
IF Kestra sends those contents to external APIs, Slack, email, or cloud services
mitigations: Restrict Kestra workflows to non-sensitive datasets
Disable or scope external connectors for sensitive jobs
Store sensitive artifacts in a segregated workspace
Add redaction before notifications and logs
Use allowlists for outbound destinations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write and shell capabilities, while LightZero has no write, shell, or git mutation capability. There is little direct overlap on mutable resources, and LightZero cannot contend for filesystem or git state. Any conflict would require an external shared resource not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator gives LightZero write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes from Kestra jobs
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Keep LightZero read-only in shared environments

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can automate downstream actions like email, Slack, PagerDuty, and cloud tasks, so if it consumes LightZero output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. LightZero is a game-playing system and may emit unverified recommendations; Kestra’s automation makes the chain operationally risky even without direct evidence of a specific parser.
conditions: IF Kestra uses LightZero output as an input to workflow decisions
IF downstream tasks execute without human verification
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any Kestra action
Require human approval for externally visible actions
Constrain LightZero output to advisory-only fields
Log and compare outputs against expected schemas
Disable auto-execution for workflows fed by model output

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling of data Kestra touches. LightZero touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not the main compliance driver. The remaining concern is Kestra’s broad handling of logs, messages, and cloud data.
conditions: IF Kestra processes regulated data classes such as logs, messages, or cloud storage data
IF those workflows route data to jurisdictions or services with stricter retention rules
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through Kestra
Keep regulated data out of notification channels
Set short retention on logs and artifacts
Document residency and retention for each workflow
